Application Materials.content:
When you apply you’ll need to submit a personal statement explaining why you want to take the course. You’ll need to include information about:
- your knowledge of the subject area
- why you want to study a postgraduate qualification in this course
- how you intend to use your qualification
References are not required for this programme. Please include the required paperwork showing your first degree and your IELTS English language test score (if you are a non-native English speaker) with your application. Without these, your application may be delayed.

Interview Requirements.content: If you don't have the exact entry requirements, but you have significant work experience in this sector we’ll assess your relevant professional experience, your subject knowledge and your aptitude for learning. Your application will be considered on individual merit and **you may be asked to attend an interview**.

Academic Requirements.content:
Typical offer: **2:1 degree**.
You’ll need a **2.1 degree** in a subject which includes quantitative study such as:
- finance
- sciences
- maths
- engineering
- computer science
- economics
- quantitative business or management
This business analytics master’s with management science is ideal for students with a background in quantitative study or work experience in this area.
We do not accept the following subjects:
- Language Studies – degrees that focus on learning a language or how to translate, such as 'Business English', 'Applied English', or 'Translation', are not acceptable. However, this restriction does not apply to ‘English’ and ‘English literature’ degrees of the kind taught in the UK.
- Art/Design/Vocational Studies – degrees that focus on learning a particular form of art, craft or vocation. These include degrees in art, graphic design, photography, television broadcasting, script writing, or performance/dance.
If you don't have the exact entry requirements, but you have significant work experience in this sector we’ll assess your relevant professional experience, your subject knowledge and your aptitude for learning. Your application will be considered on individual merit and you may be asked to attend an interview.
For applicants from China: Southampton accepts bachelor's degrees (学士学位) from China; to apply, you'll usually need the equivalent of a **2:1 or a 2:2 undergraduate degree** from a highly ranked Chinese university, with a **minimum average grade of between 70% and 83%**, depending on the university where you studied. For this course’s **2:1** requirement, Chinese equivalent entry grades are:
| Tier | GPA out of 4.0 | GPA out of 5.0 | Percentage (%) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tier A | **2.8** | **3.5** | **70%** |
| Tier B | **3.1** | **3.88** | **75%** |
| Tier C | **3.25** | **4.06** | **80%** |
| Tier D | **3.7** | **4.63** | **88%** |
If your Chinese institution isn't listed, use the grades for **tier D**.

Program Overview.content:
Business Analytics and Management Science (MSc) is a Master of Science course starting September 2026, lasting 1 year, taught full-time at Highfield Campus. With this master's, students develop skills in business analysis and learn how to gain insights from data. The degree equips students for a career in data analysis and is ideal for graduates with analytical skills who can use data to improve business performance and solve problems for organisations. It is also suited to students with a background in quantitative study or work experience in this area, and can help students specialise in further study, advance in a current professional role or change career.
The MSc teaches theory and practical application, with course content based on the latest industry practice. It is taught in partnership with the [Centre of Operational Research, Management Sciences and Information Systems (CORMSIS)](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/cormsis/), described as one of the country’s best analytics research groups. As part of CORMSIS, learning is informed by specialist research and students have a wider module choice in business and maths topics, giving them a chance to customise their postgraduate experience.
Students can either complete a dissertation or compete for a 3-month analytics summer project with an organisation, such as British Telecommunications, Deloitte or Ford. This competitive industry placement is designed to boost career prospects through a real-world challenge and a business connection. The course is taught by supportive lecturers through case studies, active discussions and practical exercises.
The course structure is full-time over 12 months, from September to the following September. In the first 9 months, semesters 1 and 2 cover the taught part of the course, made up of modules everyone takes and optional modules chosen from a list. Optional areas include advanced analytics methods such as machine learning, strategic analytics, behavioural operations, and applications of analytics in management such as finance, logistics, project and risk management, and revenue management. During semester 2 students prepare for the dissertation, then spend the final 3 months over the summer working independently to research and write it. Students also have an opportunity to compete for a 3-month summer placement in an external organisation; around 50 spaces per year are usually offered for all CORMSIS MSc students, across projects and organisations including overseas organisations such as those from China and India.
Learning develops practical skills through lectures, seminars, discussions, case studies, group work, individual reading and coursework. Students gain knowledge and understanding of IT skills through lectures, computer workshops and coursework. Speakers from different organisations visit to provide insight into how business analytics and management science are used in business, and workshops led by companies cover career-relevant topics such as report writing and skills required for summer project placements.
The dissertation gives students the opportunity to apply skills developed during the programme to a challenging problem. Students may apply for a dissertation topic set by a company or organisation, based on a real challenge they are facing, or develop their own topic. Throughout the dissertation, students work closely with an academic supervisor; if the project is with an external organisation, they also work with a representative from that organisation.
Students have access to learning and welfare services offered by the Business School and the University. A personal academic tutor offers ongoing support throughout the course, and a team of industry liaison officers can answer questions about the summer project.
Course lead: [Dr Steffen Bayer](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/people/5xhjf7/doctor-steffen-bayer), Lecturer in Business Analytics. The course is accredited by the [Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB)](https://www.aacsb.edu/).
Graduates commonly work in consultancy, technology, business, the public sector and finance. Careers directly related to this course include operational researcher, market researcher, management consultant, financial analyst, business analyst, data scientist, quantitative analyst, data analyst, risk manager and supply chain manager. Example job titles of Southampton MSc Business Analytics and Management Science graduates include data analyst, investment analyst, business analyst, management trainee, business and credit analyst, business intelligence analyst, credit risk analyst, financial analyst, management consultant and market research assistant.
Job prospects for MSc Business Analytics and Management Science graduates: £33k average professional salary; 81% in a skilled profession or further study; 95% graduate employment rate. These example graduate job titles and job prospect statistics are taken from The Graduate Outcomes Survey, which gathers information about graduates 15 months after finishing their course.

Curriculum.content:
Business Analytics and Management Science (MSc) starts in **September 2026**, lasts **1 year**, is **full-time**, and is based at **Highfield** campus.
This is a full-time master’s course. You’ll study for **12 months**, from September to the following September. In the first **9 months** (semesters 1 and 2) you'll study the taught part of your course. This is made up of modules that everyone on the course takes, and modules you choose from a list of options. During semester 2 you’ll prepare for your dissertation. For the last **3 months**, over the summer, you’ll work independently to research and write your dissertation. As part of this, you’ll have an opportunity to compete for a **3-month summer placement** in an external organisation. We usually offer around **50 spaces per year for all CORMSIS MSc students**.
You can choose optional modules to specialise in specific areas such as advanced analytics methods:
- machine learning
- strategic analytics
- behavioural operations
and the application of analytics in management:
- finance
- logistics
- project and risk management
- revenue management
For entry in academic year **2026 to 2027**, Year 1 modules you **must study**:
- [**Foundation of Business Analytics and Management Science**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6513)
- [**Optimisation and Decision Modelling**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6046)
- [**Simulation**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6122)
You **must also choose from** the following modules:
- [**Advanced Analytics**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6554)
- [**Behavioural Operations**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6555)
- [**Computational Methods for Logistics**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6542)
- [**Data Analytics and Organisational Decision Making**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6526)
- [**Dissertation (Analytics)**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6545)
- [**Financial Portfolio Theory**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6017)
- [**Principles of Risk Management**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6182)
- [**Project Management**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6537)
- [**Project Risk Management**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6143)
- [**Python for Business and Marketing**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6182)
- [**Quantitative Research in Finance**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6008)
- [**Revenue Management**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6146)
- [**Summer Project**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6546)
The dissertation gives you the opportunity to apply the skills you’ve developed during the programme to a challenging problem. You may choose to apply for a dissertation topic set by a company or organisation, based on a real challenge they are facing, or develop your own topic. Throughout your dissertation, you’ll work closely with an academic supervisor. If your project is with an external organisation, you’ll also work with a representative from that organisation.

Financial Aid.content:
Southampton Business School (MSc) Dean Scholarship (International): Scholarships of **£9,000** and **£5,000** are available to international students studying an eligible postgraduate master’s at the University of Southampton Business School, including [MSc Business Analytics and Management Science](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/business-analytics-management-science-masters-msc "MSc Business Analytics and Management Science 8516 (1 year)").
To get this scholarship you must:
- be an international student required to pay the oversees fees
- have a conditional or unconditional offer to study an eligible course
- achieve a 1st or an equivalent qualification in your undergraduate studies to receive a **£9,000** award
- achieve a 2:1 or an equivalent qualification in your undergraduate studies to receive a **£5,000** award
Students coming from China must have studied at a [Tier A](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/international/entry-qualification-equivalencies/china/postgraduate-taught-tier-list "Chinese awarding institutions listed by tier") university. There are a further 100 awards of either **£9,000** or **£5,000**, depending on applicant eligibility, for applicants coming from a [Tier B](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/international/entry-qualification-equivalencies/china/postgraduate-taught-tier-list "Chinese awarding institutions listed by tier") Chinese university. These scholarships will be issued on a first past the post basis with an additional eligibility requirement being that the applicants in this category pay their tuition fee deposit by **15th January 2026**.
You do not need to apply to this scholarship. If you meet the eligibility criteria, we will award you this scholarship and let you know by email.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
Applicants in possession of an unconditional offer of a place may request that it be deferred to the next intake. The University does not typically permit more than a single deferral. For postgraduate taught study, applicants can make a request via their online application portal and requests for deferral will typically be accepted where there are unforeseeable life events and circumstances outside of the applicants’ control.
Reasons typically accepted for deferral include: bereavement due to the loss of a close family member; serious illness and health problems; victim of a natural disaster; victim of conflict and political unrest that prohibits travel to the UK; personal accident or injury of a significant nature; child care responsibilities or caring responsibilities; relevant work experience/placements/internships; military service; change of employment circumstances; unforeseen ATAS delays; unforeseen Visa delays.
Reasons not typically accepted for deferral include: unsuccessful in securing funding (e.g. scholarship) except in cases of the Sanctuary Scholarship; to undertake employment or travel unrelated to the degree programme applied for.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
If you do not meet the English language requirements through a test or qualification, you may be able to meet them by completing one of our [pre-sessional English programmes](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/study/pre-sessional) **before you start your course**.
If you don’t meet direct entry requirements, you can apply to complete a Pre-Master's programme through Southampton's partnership with OnCampus. You'll progress to your chosen course after successfully completing the programme. [Find out more about Pre-Master's programmes for international students.](https://www.oncampus.global/our-study-centres/oncampus-southampton/progression-degrees)
